texts.preamble: Somarajan vs The State Of Kerala on 11 January, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Monday, The 11Th Day Of January 2016/21St Pousha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 755 of 2007 ( ) -------------------------------- Crl.A 274/2005 of Sessions Court,Kollam St 2009/2002 of J.M.F.C.-Iii, Punalur Revision Petitioner(S)/Appellant/Accused: -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Somarajan, S/O.Pappukutty, Puthenvila Veedu, Pannangad, Punalur. By Adv. Sri.B.Suresh Kumar Respondent(S)/State: ---------------------------------------- The State Of Kerala, Represented By The Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala Ernakulam, Representing The Food Inspector, Punalur. By Public Prosecutor, Shri.R.Githesh This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 11-01-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: B.Sudheendra Kumar, J. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - -- - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - Crl.R.P. No.755 of 2007 - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - Dated this the 11th day of January 2016 O R D E R
texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 17.5.2002 at 11 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 750 gram of 'thuvaraparippu' from the shop of the revision petitioner. After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P14 report stating that the sample consisted wholly of masurdal and therefore, the same was mis-branded. It was further stated in Ext.P14 report that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for 'thuvaraparippu' under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1956 and therefore, the same was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Exts.P1 to P20 were marked for the prosecution. DW1 was examined for the revision petitioner. 5. The courts below, solely relying on Ext. P14 report of the Public Analyst, found that the food item was misbranded and adulterated. There is no other material before the court to hold that the sample was mis-branded or adulterated.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P14 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated or misbranded. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P14 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated or misbranded in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused. Even otherwise, in view of the decision in Pepsico (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis Somarajan vs The State Of Kerala on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84841351/ 2 was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. In the result, this Revision Petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sec.2(ix)(c) read with Section 16(1)(a) of the PFA Act, 1954 and the revision petitioner is acquitted for the said offence.
